scope: Residual discovery resource-exhaustion investigation accounting for concurrent high-priority hardening. This task edited only its evidence directory; no application, live backend, account or deployment changes.
already_in_progress: Separate small discovery receivers/parser slots and one bounded large-upload slot; 16KiB actual-body cap, 2s discovery receive stall deadline and 5s small-body total deadline are present in the tested source.
One local expensive-search/Random slot, including search-bearing cursors; client error guard, Retry-After, backoff and jitter are present in the tested source.
Freshness probes are batched; frozen candidate selection is narrower and skips redundant authority joins; PostgreSQL short-search indexing and bounded cleanup changes belong to ongoing work.

findings.finding: Authentication takes the POST privacy owner lock before body/query admission. Three same-account lock waiters plus one held account transaction can occupy all four API DB connections and delay an unrelated driver.
findings.recommendation: Make discovery account contention fail promptly before it queues for an owner lock, for example a discovery-specific nonblocking owner fence or validated-account admission before the blocking fence. Preserve current revocation checks, erasure serialization and before-commit deletion checks. Do not solve this by increasing the shared DB pool alone.
findings.acceptance: Hold one account transaction; issue several same-account discovery POSTs and an unrelated authenticated read. Excess same-account requests must fail quickly without occupying the remaining pool, and account deletion must still prevent state resurrection.
findings.limits: Controlled 150ms lock-hold observation on owned PostgreSQL17, not production latency/QPS. Existing auth/discovery schema pinned at0054; current application auth/discovery code used.

findings.status: confirmed admission gaps; actual worst-case filter costs require measurement
findings.finding: Creation quotas limit new view state rather than all query execution. Eight requests using existing cursor/cached-query state entered the instrumented timeout stage again inside Retry-After, with creation quota1/minute. Duplicate same-actor/same-cursor work also entered on two replicas. Non-text filters can enter ordinary slots while the expensive gate remains unused.
findings.recommendation: Add shared per-actor work budgets for costly attempts, independent of view creation; retain cheap browsing allowance. Charge failures and cursor/Random retries. Apply a bounded server cooldown after budget exhaustion and prevent or reject duplicate work for the same actor/view/boundary across replicas. Include potentially expensive non-text filter shapes in the policy after plan measurement, and reserve capacity for ordinary reads/race traffic.
findings.acceptance: Raw clients ignoring Retry-After cannot continuously re-enter costly query work; rotate cursors/exclude/filter fields and use two replicas to confirm actor budget cannot be avoided. Include rare minimum-rating/race-history combinations and source/history holes. Keep frozen paging, uniform Random, actor scoping and genuine empty-result semantics.
findings.limits: Query work was instrumented rather than executing a costly scan. This proves admission/classification behavior, not measured PostgreSQL filter CPU cost. The generic read quota still applies; this is not a bypass of that600/minute counter.

findings.finding: An anonymous valid request containing2000 synthetic IDs matching zero source tracks returned200 with zero cards and persisted all2000 member rows. Existing per-minute member quotas and32-active-collection cap still apply.
findings.recommendation: Budget outstanding member rows/bytes per actor as well as insertion rate, and bound aggregate service intake. In bounded indexed batches, ignore IDs absent from the captured discovery population before retaining them; preserve legitimate local favorites/history and current typed collection semantics. Keep collection reuse and the expiry scheduling already being fixed.
findings.acceptance: Repeated or distinct nonexistent-ID collections do not create substantial retained state; large legitimate favorite/history sets retain the agreed50k-per-list behavior, actor privacy and bounded CPU/memory. Real existing IDs also remain subject to outstanding-state budgets.

findings.finding: Three simulated actual IPv6 peers in one/64 each obtained a fresh anonymous creation quota. Direct forwarding-header spoofing was not used; current proxy trust validation was not bypassed.
findings.recommendation: Add a secondary anonymous network/prefix abuse budget and ingress-level burst control, tuned for carrier NAT/shared networks. Keep signed-in budgets per validated player and keep cursor ownership scoped to the existing actor; do not broaden private cursor access to an entire network prefix.
findings.acceptance: Rotating actual addresses inside an attacker-controlled allocation does not reset all abuse allowances; legitimate signed-in users sharing a carrier network remain independently admitted.

findings.status: confirmed, already improved by current batching work
findings.finding: Six already-exhausted new-view attempts still issued25 SQL statements, including six batched freshness statements, before429 responses.
findings.recommendation: Consider a bounded actor/category denial hint until the rate bucket resets to avoid repeated DB rejection work, while allowing already-created cursors and cached-view semantics. This is a smaller optimization thanRE01/RE02.

negative_checks.case: Attempted small-body pool bypass with misleading Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding:chunked
negative_checks.result: Real Uvicorn/h11 accepted the framing but the actual application rejected the75019-byte body with413 before query work. Honest large Content-Length and chunked uploads used the bounded large pool. No admission-size bypass reproduced.

Per-actor read/create/member limits, fixed active-state caps, strict JSON/body bounds, HMAC cursor scope, trusted proxy handling, SQL work deadlines and current authority checks remain. No authorization bypass identified in this focused review.
